phrases.text: One job. Three people. One leader.
When a crew shares a job, HBCField counts every person on their own.
From the moment they join the job, to the moment they leave it.
And only while they are on the clock.
The office puts the crew on the job, and names the leader.
Here, Tobias leads. Priya and Conor work with him.
Everybody sees the crew card on the job: who is on it right now, since when, and who leads.
In the morning, Tobias taps On the way.
His crew get a notification: Tobias has started. One tap on I'm with him, and they are on the job too.
If all three press the same step at the same moment, all three count. Nobody loses minutes because somebody else was faster.
A join counts from the leader's start, if it comes within half an hour, and never from before your own clock-in.
With crew mode on, the leader moves the job from step to step.
The others see who does it, so nobody moves the job by accident.
The office can always step in. And with crew mode off, anybody on the crew moves the steps, as before.
At nine, the crane is late. Priya taps My issue, and writes why.
Only her time stops. It counts as blocked, for her alone.
The job, and the rest of the crew, carry on. And Tobias is told what stopped her.
When the crane arrives, she taps Back to work, and her working time runs again.
Conor is needed on another job. He taps Leave the job.
His time on this job stops. The others keep going.
When he comes back, one tap, and he counts again from that moment.
Clocking out is the same as leaving.
When one of the crew clocks out, the job carries on with the others.
Only when the last person on the job clocks out does the job pause, and nothing counts overnight.
And if the leader is sick, or simply has not clocked in? The job never waits for him.
The first person who joined, and is on the clock, stands in automatically. The card says who is standing in.
When the leader has approved leave, the office gets one notice in the morning, naming the stand-in. Keep him, or choose somebody else.
A leader can also hand the lead over himself. For today, or for good.
Only on this one job. His other jobs do not change.
And the office can change the leader, or put somebody on or off the job, with a reason that goes into the history.
At the end of the day, every person has their own line.
Tobias: eight hours of work on the job.
Priya: seven hours and twenty minutes, and forty minutes blocked, waiting for the crane.
Conor: five and a half hours. The time he spent on the other job is not counted here.
Together, twenty hours and fifty minutes of work. Counted once per person, never twice, and never more than anybody was on the clock.
The same figures go to the timesheet, the report and the invoice.
Six rules.
Each person counts from join to leave.
Only inside their own shift.
Pressing the same step together: everyone counts.
My issue stops only you.
The leader moves the steps, and somebody stands in when he is away.
The last one out pauses the job.
A crew on one job. In HBCField.
